description: Fix the four reported agentLens overlay/rendering UX defects and switch the brand accent from purple to blue. These changes are cohesive (all touch the overlay's look/behaviour plus one browser-launch fix) and share the same tests, so they are ONE feature. Preserve the overlay's non-negotiable invariant throughout: every overlay node stays pointer-events:none with zIndex 2147483646, and every server-side overlay method stays a guarded best-effort no-op that never throws into the caller or changes automation semantics (test/overlay.test.ts enforces this). Issues, mapped to code: (1) right side of the page not fully rendered = headed window/viewport mismatch in src/browser.ts; (2) synthetic cursor not visible = it starts display:none and only appears on first moveCursor; (3) streaming feedback popup is top-center and poorly styled = the banner in overlay.ts build() must move to BOTTOM-CENTER (raised up a bit) and be restyled as a modern frosted-glass card; (4) no four-corner highlight = add a NEW persistent blue four-corner bracket frame shown while Laya controls the browser.
steps: ACCENT -> BLUE (single source of truth). In src/config.ts change DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT from '#a855f7' to a blue hex (use '#3b82f6', Tailwind blue-500). Update the two env-doc comment lines that show the purple default (the LAYA_BROWSER_OVERLAY_ACCENT doc line and the 'default #a855f7' text) to the new blue value. In src/browser.ts, the disabled-overlay fallback OverlayConfig (constructor, ~line 189) hardcodes accent:'#a855f7' - import and use DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT from ./config.js instead of re-hardcoding, so there is ONE source of truth.

DERIVE SHADOWS FROM ACCENT (remove hardcoded purple rgba). In src/overlay.ts buildClientScript, the spotlight boxShadow uses rgba(168,85,247,0.25) and the ripple background uses rgba(168,85,247,0.5) - these hardcode purple and will look wrong with a blue accent. Add a tiny in-script helper that turns OPTS.accent (#rgb or #rrggbb hex) into an 'rgba(r,g,b,a)' string, and use it for the spotlight glow and the ripple fill so both track the accent automatically. Keep the fixed state colours (#22c55e success, #ef4444 error, #f59e0b uncertain) as-is; only the accent-derived purples change.

ISSUE 3 - MOVE + RESTYLE THE BANNER (bottom-center, frosted glass). In build(), change the `banner` element styles: from top:'10px'; left:'50%'; transform:'translateX(-50%)' to a BOTTOM-CENTER anchor raised up from the very bottom, e.g. bottom:'28px'; left:'50%'; transform:'translateX(-50%)' (remove the top). Restyle it into a modern glassmorphism card matching the reference: translucent light background (e.g. background:'rgba(255,255,255,0.14)'), backdropFilter:'blur(14px)' AND webkitBackdropFilter:'blur(14px)' for Safari/WebKit, a subtle blue-tinted gradient (e.g. backgroundImage a linear-gradient from a faint accent tint to transparent), border:'1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.25)', borderRadius:'16px', a soft shadow (boxShadow like '0 8px 30px rgba(0,0,0,0.18)'), and readable text colour on the translucent card (keep the existing light text but ensure contrast; a near-white title works on the frosted card). Keep the leading status dot and the small icon so it reads like the reference 'Reviewing...' card. Preserve all banner children (dot,title,stateLabel,status,progress,barWrap,meter) and their build order because tests index banner.children by position - do NOT reorder or remove children.

ISSUE 3 (cont) - MOVE THE HINT with the banner. The `hint` element ('controlled by Laya - press Esc to release') is currently top:'48px'; move it to sit just ABOVE the bottom-center banner (e.g. bottom:'70px'; left:'50%'; transform:'translateX(-50%)') so it stays visually attached to the relocated banner. Keep it translucent/subtle.

ISSUE 3 (cont) - RECONCILE bottom-corner widgets so nothing collides with the bottom-center banner. The activity-log panel (bottom-left, left:'12px'; bottom:'12px'), the WAIT countdown (bottom-right, right:'12px'; bottom:'12px'), and the scroll indicator (right:'12px'; bottom:'56px') are corner-anchored and generally clear of a centered card; verify by their left/right offsets that they do not overlap the centered banner at typical widths. If the banner's max width could reach the corners, cap the banner maxWidth (e.g. keep the existing maxWidth:'80vw' or reduce to a sensible fixed max like 'min(560px, 80vw)') so it never reaches the corner widgets. Leave the corner widgets where they are; the banner is centered and bounded.

ISSUE 2 - MAKE THE CURSOR VISIBLE AND LIVE. The synthetic `cursor` element starts display:'none' and its SVG is fill=OPTS.accent (so it becomes blue automatically once the accent is blue). Add an in-page api method `showCursor(x, y)` (or extend build/ensureRoot) that places the cursor at a default position and sets display:'block' so the cursor is present as soon as the overlay is installed, not only after the first moveCursor. Choose a sensible default position (e.g. viewport center: window.innerWidth/2, window.innerHeight/2) when no explicit coordinate is given. Keep moveCursor working exactly as before (it already sets display:'block'). Add a matching `showCursor` method on BrowserOverlay (guarded no-op like the others).

ISSUE 2 (cont) - DRIVE THE CURSOR LIVE FROM THE LOOP. In src/autopilot/loop.ts, at the start of a run (before/at the first step in runGoal, near where narrator.setState('thinking') is first called ~line 1010, or in the OverlayNarrator setup), call the new showCursor so the cursor is visibly present from the start; the existing focusTarget->moveCursor calls already move it per step, giving real-time motion. Ensure this is a guarded no-op when there is no overlay/page (reuse the OverlayNarrator `on` guard pattern).

ISSUE 4 - ADD THE FOUR-CORNER BLUE FRAME. In build(), add a NEW element (e.g. `sessionFrame`) that draws four L-shaped corner brackets at the viewport edges: a fixed, inset container (e.g. position:fixed; inset:'0' or top/left/right/bottom small insets) that is pointer-events:none, and either four child divs (one per corner) each styled with two accent-coloured borders (e.g. top-left has borderTop + borderLeft in OPTS.accent, etc.), rounded slightly, plus a soft accent glow (boxShadow using the accent-derived rgba). Start it display:'none'. Add an in-page api method `sessionFrame(on)` that toggles the frame's display between 'block' and 'none'. Add a matching `sessionFrame(page, on)` method on BrowserOverlay (guarded no-op). Ensure the frame is pointer-events:none on the container AND every corner child so it never intercepts clicks (the existing pointer-events test iterates ALL nodes under the root, so any bad node fails the suite).

ISSUE 4 (cont) - SHOW THE FRAME WHILE LAYA IS CONTROLLING. In src/autopilot/loop.ts, turn the sessionFrame ON at run start (alongside showCursor) and OFF in the terminal handlers (the success handler ~line 1390 and the error/stopped handlers ~line 1341-1401), so the blue frame is visible for the duration of an autopilot run and cleared at the end. Route it through the OverlayNarrator with the `on` guard so it is a no-op without an overlay.

ISSUE 1 - HEADED WINDOW FILLS THE VIEWPORT. In src/browser.ts launch(), keep the fixed context viewport (headless tests depend on { width, height } from options.viewport, default 1280x800) but make a HEADED Chromium launch open an OS window that matches the viewport so the page is not rendered smaller than the window (the grey strip on the right). For chromium only, when launching headed (this.options.headless === false), pass args:['--window-size=<viewport.width>,<viewport.height>'] to browserType.launch. Do NOT add the arg for headless or for firefox/webkit (they ignore/mishandle it). Keep the existing headed->headless auto-fallback intact and unchanged in behaviour; the fallback headless launch should not carry the window-size arg. Leave the context viewport as-is so all headless tests stay deterministic.

Build the client-script accent->rgba helper and any new elements so tsc still type-checks (the client script is a template string, so keep it valid JS; BrowserOverlay method signatures must be typed).
acceptance_criteria: src/config.ts DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT is a blue hex ('#3b82f6') and no comment still advertises '#a855f7' as the default.
src/browser.ts no longer hardcodes '#a855f7'; the disabled-overlay fallback uses DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT.
src/overlay.ts contains no hardcoded 'rgba(168,85,247' occurrences; the spotlight glow and ripple fill are derived from OPTS.accent.

In the injected client script the banner is anchored to the bottom (has a `bottom:` style and no `top:` on the banner) and centered (translateX(-50%)), and carries frosted-glass styling (a backdropFilter/blur and a translucent background and a borderRadius >= 12px).
The hint element is anchored near the bottom with the banner (has a `bottom:` style, not `top:'48px'`).
A four-corner frame element exists with a sessionFrame(on) api method (in-page) and a BrowserOverlay.sessionFrame(page, on) method, using the accent colour, and starts hidden.
A showCursor api method + BrowserOverlay.showCursor exist and make the cursor display:block; the loop calls showCursor and sessionFrame(true) at run start and sessionFrame(false) at run end.
src/browser.ts passes --window-size matching the viewport ONLY for headed chromium launches; headless and non-chromium launches are unchanged; the headed->headless fallback still works.

Every overlay node (including the new frame container and its corner children and the cursor) is pointer-events:none - test/overlay.test.ts 'gives every overlay node pointer-events:none' still passes.
pnpm typecheck passes and pnpm test is green after test updates in FEAT-003.
findings: Implemented all four fixes + blue accent. config.ts DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT -> #3b82f6 (env-doc comments updated). browser.ts: disabled-overlay fallback now imports DEFAULT_OVERLAY_ACCENT; headed CHROMIUM launch passes args:['--window-size=W,H'] matching viewport (headless + firefox/webkit never get it; headed->headless fallback re-launches WITHOUT the arg, verified in fallback test log which shows --window-size only on the initial headed attempt). overlay.ts: added in-script accentRgba(alpha) hex->rgba helper; spotlight boxShadow + ripple background now derive from OPTS.accent (no more rgba(168,85,247...)); banner moved from top:10px to bottom:28px, restyled frosted glass (rgba(255,255,255,0.14) bg + accent-tinted linear-gradient, backdropFilter+webkitBackdropFilter blur(14px), borderRadius 16px, boxShadow 0 8px 30px, border rgba white, maxWidth min(560px,80vw)); banner child order preserved. hint moved to bottom:70px. Added showCursor(x,y) api (defaults to viewport centre, display:block) + sessionFrame(on) api drawing four L-shaped accent corner brackets (container + 4 children all pointer-events:none), starts hidden. Added BrowserOverlay.showCursor + BrowserOverlay.sessionFrame guarded no-ops. loop.ts Narrator gained showCursor()+sessionFrame(on); runGoal calls showCursor()+sessionFrame(true) after navigation at run start and sessionFrame(false) in BOTH terminal paths (catch block + normal end after hideSpotlight). Verification: pnpm typecheck clean; grep 'rgba(168,85,247' src/overlay.ts -> none; grep 'a855f7' src/config.ts src/browser.ts -> none; pnpm build clean; full pnpm test 247 passed / 3 skipped (webkit self-skips, no display server). Tests updated to keep suite green (this covers FEAT-003's needs): config.test.ts default+garbage-fallback accent -> #3b82f6; overlayOn() accent literal -> #3b82f6 in overlay.test.ts + tier3-ux.test.ts; added two new overlay.test.ts cases asserting bottom-anchored frosted banner+hint and visible cursor + 4-corner pointer-events:none frame toggle. No display server so headed visuals could not be eyeballed; verified via injected-script DOM assertions + tsc as instructed.
